correctness.rationale: The dot and cross products with (x,y) give r'=r^3(-a+b cos 2theta) and theta'=r^2. Thus r^2=C exp(-2a theta+b sin 2theta). Independently integrating the inverse angular speed from minus infinity gives I'(theta)=exp(2a theta-b sin 2theta)>0; I is comparable to exp(2a theta) and is onto (0,infinity). The full forward orbit has I(theta)=C(t+D) with D=I(theta0)/C>0, and (t+D)r^2=I/I'=F evaluated at theta(t). The half-turn shifts log I by 2 pi a, so the angular quotient defines a positive smooth periodic function of log I. Replacing t+D by t perturbs the phase and factor by O(t^-1), by boundedness of the profile and its derivative. F'=1+(2b cos 2theta-2a)F rules out a constant when b is nonzero; b=0 gives 1/(2a). Monotone advance in log t gives every value in the continuous image of a period as an accumulation point, and ordinary periodic Cesaro averaging after u=log t gives the stated occupation law for bounded continuous tests. The polar solution exists globally and r(t)<=r0 exp(|b|), giving stability even for orbits with transient radial growth. The package checker was inspected, not executed; its finite quadratures are not the proof.
residual_risks: No minimal-period assertion is required; only the guaranteed period was audited here.
